intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that recurrent hydatidiform mole-6 (HYDM6) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the KASH5 gene (618125) on chromosome 19q13.33.

paragraphs.text: Recurrent hydatidiform mole-6 (HYDM6) is an autosomal recessive female reproductive disorder in which affected women have recurrent hydatidiform moles. Reported patients have also had miscarriages, and in one family, recurrent or metastatic gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN).

paragraphs.text: Rezaei et al. (2024) performed whole-exome sequencing in 75 unrelated patients with recurrent hydatidiform moles who were negative for recessive mutations in NLRP7 and KHDC3L. They found deleterious biallelic variants in genes involved in meiosis I in patients with recurrent androgenetic complete moles. All 6 moles that were genotyped were androgenetic and monospermic. In a Jordanian woman (patient 439) with 3 hydatidiform moles and 2 miscarriages, they found 2 heterozygous variants in the KASH5 gene: a c.1555C-T transition, causing an arg519-to-ter (R519X) substitution, and a c.1604T-A transversion, causing a leu535-to-gln (L535Q) substitution. Only the R519X variant was inherited from her mother, so the authors concluded that the 2 variants were most likely on different parental chromosomes. In the same study, Rezaei et al. (2024) found biallelic variants in other meiotic genes in other patients, including HFM1 (615684), MAJIN (617130), SYCP2 (604105), and MEIOB (617670).

paragraphs.text: Saharan et al. (2026) performed whole-exome sequencing in 2 women with recurrent hydatidiform moles. In one patient, who had recurrent gestational trophoblastic neoplasia, they found a very rare homozygous arg196-to-his (R196H) variant in the KASH5 gene. Her sister also had recurrent moles and died of metastatic GTN. The authors stated that their findings further supported an association between variants in this gene and recurrent moles.

paragraphs.text: Rezaei et al. (2024) compared 15 patients who had recurrent androgenetic moles and biallelic pathogenic variants in 9 meiosis-related genes with 70 patients who had no biallelic variants. The 15 patients had more severe reproductive outcomes: 1 live birth and 62 pregnancy losses, compared with 39 live births and 198 losses in the 70 patients (P = 0.0007).

checks.claim: Rezaei et al. (2024) compared 15 patients with recurrent androgenetic moles and biallelic pathogenic variants in 9 meiosis-related genes with 70 patients who had no biallelic variants.
checks.evidence_quote: Comparing the reproductive outcomes of all our patients with androgenetic RHM and recessive P/LP variants in the 9 genes (n = 15 patients) with those of patients who had remained negative (n = 70) for biallelic P/LP variants

checks.claim: The 15 patients with biallelic pathogenic variants in meiosis-related genes had more severe reproductive outcomes than the 70 patients without biallelic variants.

checks.claim: The 15 patients with biallelic meiosis-gene variants had 1 live birth and 62 pregnancy losses.

paragraphs.text: Rezaei et al. (2024) suggested that recurrent androgenetic complete moles may be a sign of accelerated ovarian aging, or a milder form of premature ovarian insufficiency. They noted that this would explain why androgenetic moles become more common with advanced maternal age.

checks.claim: Rezaei et al. (2024) suggested that recurrent androgenetic complete moles may be a sign of accelerated ovarian aging, or a milder form of premature ovarian insufficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: The data from our study suggest that recurrent AnCHM may be a sign of accelerated ovarian aging or a milder form of POI before its manifestation by clinical and laboratory tests.

checks.claim: Rezaei et al. (2024) noted that accelerated ovarian aging would explain why androgenetic moles become more common with advanced maternal age.
checks.evidence_quote: Our data link POI to the pathology of RHM and provide an explanation for the increased incidence of common AnCHM with advanced maternal age.

paragraphs.text: In a Jordanian woman (patient 439) with recurrent hydatidiform moles (HYDM6), who had had 3 hydatidiform moles and 2 miscarriages, Rezaei et al. One was a c.1555C-T transition (NM_144688), resulting in an arg519-to-ter (R519X) substitution, which she had inherited from her mother. The other was a c.1604T-A transversion, resulting in a leu535-to-gln (L535Q) substitution. The authors concluded that the 2 variants were most likely on different parental chromosomes.
